column2: Playing tip to deploy sea mines:
1. Deploy first your ground units and exit the deployment screen.
2. Select a mine layer ship then click on the "deploy forces" button, only then you can deploy sea mines wherever you move the ship at any game turn.
Excellent! The campaign has reached its end!
Note: your duty was better than the historic one, Congratulations and thanks for playing!
We have lost our three divisions here!!! they have been unarmed into Spain, this is a completely disaster!. A military council is waiting for you in Germany.

This is the last battle to complete your campaign in the Afrikan's West, the fortified City of Casablanca! The city is surrounded by mine fields and fortitications, in the ocean the Angloamerican Navy is awesome and the RAF has used all its forces from bases in Gibraltar, but we trust you and we believe that you'll find the way to avoid all these obtacles in this struggle and kick-out the allies from this sector of Afrika.
Very Good! you'd demonstrate clearly your superiority, now is time to advance towards Algeria.
You couldn't make allies to get back in Tunisia, so it's impossible to defend Alexandria and Tunisia with the few units we have.
We know that you've recently arrived from El Alamein but the severity of the situation right here demand your services.
After Angloamerican's disembarks in the Afrikan coasts they'd surround us. Due to our lack of forces we failed to resist in battle.
Your mission: show the enemy that we are no defeated, advance quickly towards the inner Tunes to create a chaos within their armies.
Your efforts have been very meritorious, but the Americans have broken the line in El Guettar, so we don't have another choice: the retreat.
Excellent!! You have captured the oil reserves located in Tebessa!
Your next assignment will be: try to enclose the Angloamerican armies which are currently in Bone.
London'44 - January 5th, 1944
The city of London still resist to our efforts Herr General. We need your intervention to take the city and end British resistance for good!!!
The Angloamerican forces have disembarked in French territory, at full speed following a route to Tunisia, after your defeat in Egypt, this is the only defendible sector of Afrika that we have left.
Due to the unexperienced rivals, their positions are badly defended, but they outnumbered you easily and have more supplies. Your mission: Advance at full speed and take Tebessa.
Note: In Tebessa, the allies used to have a great oil reserve, if you capture it, we could proceed to future offensive operations.
The Angloamerican attempt to surprise us from behind was a complete failure, now we can concentrate on fight agaisnt Monty in the Mareth Line.
You have failed to force allies to retreat in Tunisia, so it's impossible to defend Tunisia with the few units we have.
Thanks to you great successes, now we have the possibility to surround the rookie armies going to the Tunisian coast, more exactly, the city of Bone.
If you are successful, they won't have any choice but surrender.
Excellent! after this great victory, the 8th army won't be able to make a quick reorganization, this is our chance to take the iniciative, we will chase the Allies toward west.
You couldn't force allies to get back in Tunis, so it's impossible to attack with the few units we have.
March 6th, 1943

After West front destruction, you are facing your most difficult duty, once more battle against the Monty's 8th, this is a very difficult mission, but if you are successful you will have stopped the menace of our expulsion from Afrika.
Note: this was the last operation commanded by Rommel in the Afrikan arena.
November 7, 1943
The Soviets cross the middle Dnepr river at the junction between Army
Groups Center and South.

We are facing a terrible situation, the 8th Army is going to attack our last bastion and our scout units reported that Monty has sent the 2nd division NZ through the mountains, at the same time, he is going to launch a full frontal attack against our lines.
Avoid his success at all costs!

We have fought until the end, we don't have fuel, ammo neither equipment or food, however the Führer has formally forbidden to evacuate Afrika, so we must ask you to do the better you can under those circumstances.
German Campaign: 1941-????
Equipment: DAK E-File or European E-File
Gameset: DAK or Germany West

In 1941 the Italian Army was unable to face the Brits in Africa. After a year of disasters, they called for help to his German allies. Germany couldn't bring free hands to the British in North Africa, and in February 12th of 1941 they sent the General Rommel with the first German equipment and men to Tripoli.
Can you manage the Deutsches Afrika-Korps to the victory, and overcome the Rommel's achievements in Africa ?

Excellent job. Again 100,000s of Russians are trapped in pockets behind our lines. The Bolsheviks made the mistake of committing all their troops to the first line of defense. Once you broke through, they had no reserve forces to stop you. Partisan activity makes it  increasingly difficult to operate from the airfields close to the front (That's why the airfields did not offer resupply). Now it's time to move East. Moscow is the target.

We are not on schedule, but again 100,000s of Russians are trapped in pockets behind our lines. The Bolsheviks made the mistake of committing all their troops to the first line of defense. Your forces have been stopped. Capturing Moscow before winter will become very difficult now.

Your inability to capture your objectives in and around Moscow has led to disaster. The Soviet armies, reinforced by troops from Siberia have wreaked havoc on our overextended and once invincible armies. Fierce Soviet counterattacks this winter have put back our weary troops all along the front.

Congratulations Herr General. You have broken through the Russian defenses and have ran into and crushed the lead elements of the 5th Guards Tank Army. Next stop on the way to Kursk is the village of Prokhorovka.

Congratulations Herr General. You have broken through the Russian defenses and have ran into and beaten the lead elements of the 5th Guards Tank Army. Next stop on the way to Kursk is the village of Prokhorovka.

Not only here, but also at multiple other locations, the Bolsheviks have crossed the Mius. Kharkov is now under severe Russian pressure. Send your troops to the Kharkov area to safeguard the city. Your well-trained Panther battalion will join you shortly.

It took quite some effort, but the bolshevik bidgehead has been crushed. Unfortunately Russian forces have crossed the Mius at multiple other locations. Kharkov is now under severe Russian pressure. Send your troops to the Kharkov area to safeguard the city. Your well-trained Panther battalion will join you shortly.

You have inflicted great tank losses on the 5GTA and you held on to Kharkov. However, Russian advances North and South of the city force us to retreat to the Dniepr. Most of your forces are sent to France for rest and refit. Only a Kampfgruppe will remain on the Eastern front until the spring of 1944.

The Fourth Battle of Kharkov - August 28th, 1943

The Russian 5th Guards tank army that got badly mauled at Prokhorovka when meeting your forces in mid July has been rebuilt, rushed through the gap between our 4th Pz Army and Group Kempf and is now threatening Kharkov. A field marshal's baton, engraved with your name awaits your arrival at Number 10.  I shall personally be there with the PM for the ceremony.  A spot of tea, Commander?
Well Herr General, despite harsh conditions, you have done quite well!
Your victory has shown that already you have gained valuable
experience in this new type of warfare.  In addition, the new pro-German
government in Spain may prove to be a useful ally in the coming years.
Herr General, we have an excellent opportunity to deliver a crushing blow to the enemy, here, north of Strasbourg. As you can see, the advance of the American Third Army has left this sector of

Good Work!, the British resistance into the streets of Bristol has been really hard, but finally you did it, now we have the control of the whole South East coast of England, the Allies can't sent supplies for the British anymore.

Excellent!, we have cleared of enemies the Somme River, and Amiens has fallen into our hands. Now we must continue closing the encirclement, driving to the North, to Arras, where the British have sent some divisions.
Minsk 1946 - May 12th, 1946

Commander, Stalin has turned the city of Minsk into a fortress. We need your skills to take the city. This is not going to be easy commander, the Russians are heavily entrenched and abundently supplied. You will have a little less than three weeks to complete this mission.
Due to your failure you are out of charge and you will not command another operation in this campaign. The Allies have taken the Gustav Line and there are no defenses available until the Balcanes.
England Midlands - April 3th, 1944
Strock: Herr General, the British have concentrated their last reserves in the Midlands. A victory here will be their doom!! End British resistance for good!!!
Congratulations Comrade, Italy has surrendered to us and there's only
a few allied resistance groups that will be crushed soon.
Reports confirm that the French Campaign was successful, now
we can force the allies to surrender.
Excellent! You will figure in the history books! You have destroyed the beachhead in Anzio! Now we can concentrate all our forces at the Gustav Line.
You have disgraced the Allied forces, and on a more specific note, the British Army. You are being sent on a rather long leave. Enjoy your leisure years.
Comrade General you have fought bravely throughout all German attacks! Unfortunately the city is mostly in German hands. Our situation is very precarious!
Mersa Matruh - February 1st, 1946
The enemy has regrouped and launched a counter offensive against our quickly erected defenses.  You must immediately repel the attack and continue our Egyptian campaign to eliminate the Americans.
Thanks to you we've got Ivan on the run.
The Germans try to break through the Anglo-French lines and capture
the French city of Dunkirk.
Good job Commander. Although Greece has fallen, those submarines have been destroyed and Allied shipping is safe.

With the help of their German ally, Finland tries to retake what was lost to the Soviets a year earlier.

You know, Commander, if we're ever going to win this war, we need people who do more than just punch the clock.  You took St. Lo, yeah, but it cost us, not just time, but GIs.  It's been decided, we're going to give you another chance - in Caen.  Make your country proud, Commander.

Paris is in panic!, our divisions are driving into France quickly, and the Allied army is in a complete disarray. Herr General, your task now will consist in secure this area in order to allow the drive of our spearheads into the French soil. This, will avoid the joining of the Allied forces in the North, with the Southern allied forces, and will cut the Allied controlled space in two.
Viel Gluck!, we need a complete victory here to continue the drive to the French Channel..

The 26 and the 47 infanterie divisions are already taking positions around the Somme River, which is a possible bridgehead. Your mission is to deploy your forces here to aid in the crossing of the Somme River. Amiens is the biggest objective of your mission. Intelligence reports show that the garrison of Amiens consist only of one BEF regiment, but personally, I know the Frenchs will fight hard trying to avoid the crossing of the Somme.
Comrade General you have failed to break the lines on the flanks of Sixth Army! We cannot expelled the Germans now! Vassiliev is very upset with your incompetence!

After the victory in Amiens, our Panzer forces are taking positions to attack Arras, where some units from the 1st French Army are deployed, as well as some BEF forces. The 7th Panzer division of the General Rommel is available to support the attack (in fact we didn't know where really was this division), and also the SS Division "Totenkopf", and other Wehrmacht units which will arrive later. We expect a complete victory here.
St, Pol-s T.
Champagne-les H.

Finally we have reached the Channel. The enemy forces are trying to delay our advance while they are embarking their units in the port of Dünkirchen. We have spent a precious time in the ordered pause by OKH, but we will destroy all the forces enclosed in our trap, if we can make a fast assault on the enemy positions.

After our Blitz advance over Duenkirchen, the remnants of the Allied forces are enclosed arond the Ypres Channel and the city of Lille. Your mission is to end with the enemy resistance as soon as possible, by attacking from the South, taking Lille, and the another mission objective.

The enemy airforce is completely destroyed, so our Stukas can work without any opposition, and bomb the enemy positions easily. We expect a fast and complete victory here which allow us to get the complete surrender of the French forces.
Ebro - November 2nd, 1938

Feldmarschall Strock (Assistant Chief of Staff): Good day, Herr Oberst. Due to our need to expand our forces, you have been selected to train a group of young infantry school graduates. To get them started, you will assist our Nationalist friends in Spain at the river Ebro. Good luck.
Gerona - January 31st, 1939
Feldmarschall Strock (Assistant Chief of Staff): Good day, Herr Oberst. After your victory you can assist our Nationalist friends in Spain at the city of Gerona. Good luck.

Strock: Let me be the first to congratulate you on your promotion, Herr General! We are very pleased by your performance. I know you deserve to celebrate, but keep it short, you'll need your rest. You have a long day ahead of you tomorrow.

Strock: Herr General, we have a pressing situation with Poland. For months now, the Führer has been trying to negotiate with them a generous settlement regarding Katowitz and Danzig. Since they have numerous allies on their side, including England, they have been very unreasonable and unrelenting in their demands. Several days ago, they have gotten so arrogant that they crossed our border at several places. The Führer felt obligated that in order to preserve the freedom of our citizens, we have to strike back. I want you to go forth with such force that they, and any future aggressors, will see that we will not be pushed into submission.
Comrade General: You will command the Second Baltic Front in charge of liberating the city of Riga and most of Latvia!
Tolvajarvi - December 9th, 1939

Strock: Herr General, here is another opportunity for you and your men to gain valuable battlefield experience. The Soviet Union has invaded Finland, and Finland has requested our help. You will meet with Colonel Talvela at Tolvajarvi to assist him at repelling their enemy. Because we basically gave Finland to the Soviet Union, you and your men will go only as volunteers. If you are captured, the German government will deny the legitimacy of your identity.

Major von Beck (Intelligence Officer): Sir, several of Colonel Talvela's units are isolated. Luckily, they have somewhat entrenched themselves and can hold out for some time in case they get discovered. We also have a unit of Fallschirmjager due to arrive in approximately six hours to assist them.
Strock: Herr General, the Soviets are withdrawing in disarray! You achieved a great victory!
St. Quentin - May 14th, 1940

Strock: Herr General, the French have discovered that our west wall is weak, and numerous confrontations have erupted between our border guards and their patrols. The Fuhrer has decided to solve this problem in the same manner as the Polish campaign, and we have to do this now. Because as time passes, the Allies get stronger. Good luck.

von Beck: Sir, there are enemy anti-aircraft batteries and at least two enemy fighter units operating in the area. For support, we are receiving a fighter and a bomber unit, which are due to arrive in eight hours. Additional infantry support is delayed and won't be arriving for another two and a half days.
Strock: Due to your success in this campaign, the French are now on the run. Good job!
Somme - June 5th, 1940
Herr General, we are now at the second stage of our French campaign. Our victory here will cut off the French from their British allies. Good luck to you.
Strock: Herr General, despite the enemy resistance you have destroyed the enemy factory!!
Sidi Barrani - September 13rd, 1940

Strock: Herr General, Mussolini has requested your guidance, along with several reconnaissance, panzer, and artillery units to assist him in Egypt. Furthermore, since our Luftwaffe can deploy very quickly, you can bring all of your available aircraft. You and your detachment won't be away long and the rest will stay as a contingency force. This will be a great opportunity for some of your units to gain valuable battlefield experience. Good luck to you.

von Beck: Sir, there is a fighter unit and a bomber unit that are six hours away and two unmotorized infantry units that are about fourteen hours away to reinforce us. Other than those, the Italians have no more forces to commit.
Strock: Excellent work, Herr General. You have stopped the British offensive!
Benghazi - January 24th, 1941
Strock: Herr General, due your success at Sidi Barrani, Mussolini once again requests your guidance. This time, it is to recapture Benghazi in Cyrenaica. Good luck.
von Beck: Sir, there are additional enemy fighters on the way to add to what they currently have. They are several days away, but exactly how many days, we don't know.

Strock: Excellent work, Herr General. Now, you and your reconnaisance crew need to do your celebrating in my plane, and your Luftwaffe needs to get rest right away for their journey to Berlin tomorrow. All of us have to get there ASAP. There, you will be briefed on the next mission. You are going to England!
Glasgow - March 13th, 1941
